BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.verification: Read setup at source lines 123-208 and the three cited results. Source uses positive entries and one-sided shifts. Absolute values, natural extension and axis symmetry justify the broader signed/two-sided formulation and extra decompositions. No separation condition is needed for the cited Section 1 assertions. Source-derived statement, not verbatim transcription.
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.exact_lean_declaration:
def FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition : Prop :=
  ∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] (S : System ι),
    S.WithRotations → S.HasProximalDiagonal → ∀ {s : ℝ}, 0 < s → s < 2 →
    ∀ (μ : Measure (ℤ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ], MeasurePreserving (shift 1) μ μ →
    S.HasGibbsBounds s μ → ∃ μ₁ μ₂ : Measure (ℤ → ι × ZMod 2), S.GibbsDecomposition s μ μ₁ μ₂
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.gibbs_existence: The existence of the ergodic Gibbs measures on the mixing Sigma_Z is Bowen's theorem, which the library proves with no literature input (bowenGibbsExistence, existsUnique_ergodic_isGibbsPotential, BoxLike/Bowen/); the proof of the predicate starts from it (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁).
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.proof: Bowen's theorem (bowenGibbsExistence) gives the ergodic Gibbs measure μ₁ for f_{1,s} on the mixing Σ_Z (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁), and μ₂ is its image under the exchange of the axes (System.isGibbs_potential₂_map_flipAxis); the image of μ₁ under forgetting the axis has the Gibbs bounds of φ^s, since each word has two lifts and φ^s(A_w) is the larger of the two exponentials (System.hasGibbsBounds_map_unCode); every invariant measure with the Gibbs bounds equals this ergodic measure (System.eq_of_hasGibbsBounds); the four decompositions follow from Σ_Z = τ(Σ) ⊔ ω(Σ) and the exchange of the two ranges; the Lyapunov identities follow from Birkhoff's theorem along the two lifts and the relative-entropy comparison \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₂) ≤ \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₁) (System.lyapunov_map_unCode_of_isGibbs).

BoxLike.PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.exact_statement: Universally over finite discrete alphabets and planar self-affine systems P (PlanarSystem: invertible contracting linear parts): for a shift-invariant ergodic probability mu with lambda2 < lambda1, mu.map P.proj is exact-dimensional of dimension (h1-h0)/lambda1 + (h2-h1)/lambda2, with hi = P.dimEntropy mu i.
BoxLike.PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.citation: Feng, Dimension of invariant measures for affine iterated function systems, Duke Math. J. 172 (2023), Theorems 1.2 (ii) and 1.3, formula (1.6)
BoxLike.PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.verification: Compared with arXiv:1901.01691v2 (2 June 2020), Theorem 1.2 (ii) and Theorem 1.3, formula (1.6). The full source boundary record is the docstring of the definition.
BoxLike.PlanarFengLedrappierYoung.source_boundary: Source: an affine IFS on R^d, not necessarily invertible or contracting; an ergodic m on the two-sided full shift for which the system is average contracting; the distinct Lyapunov exponents with multiplicities k_i; local dimensions with closed Euclidean balls; the entropies h_i = H_m(P | xi_i-hat) of (1.5). Specialisation: d = 2, invertible contractions, mu ergodic with lambda2 < lambda1, so that s = 2, k_1 = k_2 = 1 and (1.6) is (h1-h0)/lambda1 + (h2-h1)/lambda2. Feng's entropies for his partitions on a Borel set of full measure inside the library's Sigma' are the library's (PlanarSystem.condEntropy_fengXi_eq), so the source statement implies the transcription (planarFengLedrappierYoung_of_fengXi, proved). Closed supremum-norm balls give the same pointwise dimension as Euclidean balls; the order of the matrix products and the signs agree with Feng's (1.3), Section 1.2 and (1.6). Degenerate instances, by hand: one letter with A = diag(1/2, 1/4) (Dirac projection, all h_i = 0); zero translations with a Bernoulli measure (both sides 0); scaled rotations (lambda1 = lambda2, the statement is silent).

BoxLike.KittleKoglerDimension.exact_statement: For every finite alphabet kappa, ratios r_j != 0 with |r_j|<1, real translations t_j, positive real weights p_j summing to one, and injective simWord r t: every stationary probability nu with nu=sum_j ofReal(p_j) times (x -> r_j*x+t_j)_*nu is exact-dimensional with min(1,sum_j negMulLog(p_j)/(-sum_j p_j log|r_j|)).
BoxLike.KittleKoglerDimension.verification: Read source setup, exact-dimensionality convention, Theorem 1.1 and the explicit free-semigroup entropy observation. The source theorem uses random-walk entropy; freeness gives Shannon entropy. Injectivity implies distinct generators, and the empty word is harmless for strict contractions. Stationary-probability uniqueness in source explains universal quantification over nu. This is a faithful specialisation, not a proof of the source theorem.
BoxLike.KittleKoglerDimension.exact_lean_declaration:
def KittleKoglerDimension : Prop :=
  ∀ {κ : Type u} [Fintype κ] (r t p : κ → ℝ), (∀ j, r j ≠ 0) → (∀ j, |r j| < 1) →
    (∀ j, 0 < p j) → ∑ j, p j = 1 → Function.Injective (simWord r t) →
    ∀ (ν : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν],
    ν = ∑ j, ENNReal.ofReal (p j) • ν.map (fun x => r j * x + t j) →
    IsExactDim ν (min 1 ((∑ j, Real.negMulLog (p j)) / -(∑ j, p j * Real.log |r j|)))

def BaranyKaenmakiTheorem : Prop :=
  ∀ η : ℕ → ℝ, Antitone η → (∀ n, 0 < η n) →

    ¬ {p : ℝ × ℝ | 0 < p.1 ∧ p.1 < 1 / 3 ∧ 0 < p.2 ∧ p.2 < p.1 / (1 - p.1) ∧ HomFree p.1 p.2 ∧

BoxLike.FengKaenmakiUnique.name: BoxLike.FengKaenmakiUnique
BoxLike.FengKaenmakiUnique.content: Two invariant equilibrium probability measures of an irreducible box-like System coincide.
BoxLike.FengKaenmakiUnique.exact_lean_declaration:
def FengKaenmakiUnique : Prop :=
  ∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι] (S : System ι),
    S.Irreducible → ∀ {s : ℝ}, 0 < s → s < 2 →
    ∀ (μ μ' : Measure (ℤ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure μ'],
    MeasurePreserving (shift 1) μ μ → MeasurePreserving (shift 1) μ' μ' →
    S.IsEquilibriumState s μ → S.IsEquilibriumState s μ' → μ = μ'

BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.exact_statement: Universally over finite discrete alphabets: for an irreducible tuple A of invertible real 2x2 matrices (TupleIrreducible A, det A_i != 0) and q>0, every shiftPlus-invariant probability measure nu on the one-sided shift that is a q-equilibrium state of the norm potential (IsNormEquilibriumPlus A q nu) has the Gibbs property HasNormGibbsPlus A q nu and is the only invariant q-equilibrium state.
BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.citation: Feng-Kaenmaki, Equilibrium states of the pressure function for products of matrices, Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. 30 (2011), Proposition 1.2
BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.verification: Proposition 1.2 read in arXiv:1009.3129v1 (16 September 2010), p. 3, with its setting on pp. 1-2; the journal version was not consulted. The full source boundary record is the docstring of the definition.
BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.source_boundary: Source: F = R or C, d x d matrices irreducible over F^d (their Definition 1.1), the one-sided full shift, P(q) of their (1.1) with the standard matrix norm, M_*(mu) of (1.2), q-equilibrium states by (1.4); conclusion: for each q>0 a unique q-equilibrium state mu_q with the Gibbs property (1.6), and P'(q) = M_*(mu_q). Specialisation: F = R, d = 2, invertible matrices, the l2 operator norm (all norms give the same P, M_* and equilibrium states, and the Gibbs property with another constant), entropy entropyPlus of the generating partition, P and M_* as limUnder of convergent sequences (MatrixTuple.tendsto_normPressure, MatrixTuple.tendsto_normLyapPlus, tendsto_entropyPlus). Weaker than the source: no existence of mu_q (proved: MatrixTuple.exists_isEquilibriumState), the Gibbs property for n >= 1 only, no differentiability of P, no singular matrices (for which P(q) = -inf is possible and Real.log 0 = 0 would make a transcription false). Degenerate instances: the empty alphabet is not irreducible, so the statement is silent; for the one-letter tuple of the quarter turn the conclusion is proved (FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.degenerate_quarterTurn).

BoxLike.FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium.downstream_uses: MatrixTuple.irred_eq_state_of_fengKaenmaki (Proposition 3.10, thm:irred_eq_state, at the article's scope) and the reductions above; no headline result.

def FengKaenmakiNormEquilibrium : Prop :=
  ∀ {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace ι] [MeasurableSingletonClass ι]
    (A : ι → Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℝ), (∀ i, (A i).det ≠ 0) → TupleIrreducible A →
    ∀ {q : ℝ}, 0 < q → ∀ (ν : Measure (ℕ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν],
    MeasurePreserving shiftPlus ν ν → MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibriumPlus A q ν →
    MatrixTuple.HasNormGibbsPlus A q ν ∧
      ∀ (ν' : Measure (ℕ → ι)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ν'], MeasurePreserving shiftPlus ν' ν' →
        MatrixTuple.IsNormEquilibriumPlus A q ν' → ν' = ν

BoxLike.System.RossiBound.exact_statement: For the given box-like system S, every ergodic invariant probability mu satisfies upperHausdorffDim (pi_* mu) <= min 2 (lyapDim (entropy mu) (lyapunov1 mu) (lyapunov2 mu)).
BoxLike.System.RossiBound.verification: Stated for the background sentence eq:hausdorff_ergodic_lyapunov and taken by no theorem: the proof of Theorem 4.16 evaluates Feng's formula to an equality. Equality in the bound for the equilibrium state is proved (System.upperHausdorffDim_map_proj_eq).
BoxLike.System.RossiBound.exact_lean_declaration:
def RossiBound : Prop :=
  ∀ μ : Measure (ℤ → ι), IsProbabilityMeasure μ → Ergodic (shift 1) μ →
    upperHausdorffDim (μ.map S.proj) ≤
      min 2 (lyapDim (entropy μ) (S.lyapunov₁ μ) (S.lyapunov₂ μ))

entries.label: thm:fraser
entries.other_hypotheses: Finite nonempty box-like contractive invertible affine IFS; ROSC for second and third conclusions; Both coordinate projections have Minkowski dimension one for third conclusion
